boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a plural summons, שִׁמְע֣וּ אֶת הַדָּבָ֗ר (oshb:Jer.10.1, byte), matching “Hear the word which Yahweh speaks to you, house of Israel!” (web:Jer.10.1). A koh-amar onset follows at once, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.10.2, byte), placing the opening idol mockery in Yahweh's own mouth. The speech does not hold a single mouth for its whole length: a second-person address praising Yahweh directly breaks in, מֵאֵ֥ין כָּמ֖וֹךָ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל אַתָּ֛ה (oshb:Jer.10.6, byte) — “There is no one like you, Yahweh. You are great,” (web:Jer.10.6) — continued at מִ֣י לֹ֤א יִֽרָאֲךָ֙ (oshb:Jer.10.7, byte); a third-person predication about Yahweh follows at וַֽיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ אֱמֶ֔ת (oshb:Jer.10.10, byte); and the address returns to the plural nations addressees at the Aramaic close. No fresh koh-amar onset, addressee-naming imperative, or discourse frame opens a rival unit at any of these turns, so the alternation of mockery, praise addressed to Yahweh, and predication about Yahweh is read as one continuous speech rather than divided at these internal turns. It closes on an Aramaic sentence, כִּדְנָה֙ תֵּאמְר֣וּן לְה֔וֹם אֱלָ֣הַיָּ֔א דִּֽי שְׁמַיָּ֥א וְאַרְקָ֖א לָ֣א עֲבַ֑דוּ (oshb:Jer.10.11, byte) — “You shall say this to them: ‘The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth, and from under the heavens.’” (web:Jer.10.11) — a self-contained Aramaic island inside the surrounding Hebrew, functioning as the refutation formula Israel is told to hand back to the nations; the opening verb is a prefix-conjugation form with the paragogic nun, rendered as a modal future rather than an imperative, and it belongs with the preceding mockery. The row is cut here because verse 12 opens a distinct hymnic unit in Hebrew rather than continuing this address.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the second-person praise addressed to Yahweh, or the third-person predication about Yahweh, out of the surrounding idol mockery into separate rows was rejected because no koh-amar onset, addressee-naming imperative, or discourse frame marks a fresh seam at any of these turns; the mockery, the praise, and the predication interleave inside the same continuous speech.
literature_type_guess: idol polemic with interleaved praise and an embedded refutation formula

boundary_rationale: Where the Aramaic sentence just before it argues from what the nations' gods did not do, this unit pivots to what Yahweh did do: a participial hymn opening, עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֨רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ (oshb:Jer.10.12, byte), matching “God has made the earth by his power.” (web:Jer.10.12). It closes on the name-formula, יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.10.16, byte) — “Yahweh of Armies is his name.” (web:Jer.10.16) — byte-identical to the same formula closing oshb:Jer.51.19, the closing verse of this hymn's twin at Jer.51.15-Jer.51.19; the wider twin pairing is held here as texture rather than as the warrant for this edge, and it does not hold at a single tier throughout — two of the five paired verses are byte-identical (oshb:Jer.10.12 and oshb:Jer.51.15; oshb:Jer.10.15 and oshb:Jer.51.18) while the other three diverge already in their consonants.
